_readme: Standard British isolated phonemes - HUMAN recordings, one consistent
reference voice. This manifest is production tooling only; it never ships
(tools/ is excluded from the deployed artifact). It is also the file
tools/prep_phonemes.py reads to know the order and the names, so a session
cannot be prepped without it.
Workflow: record each entry -> name the file <slug>.mp3 -> run
python3 tools/prep_phonemes.py <folder> --manifest tools/phoneme_manifest_ssbe.json --out prepped/
python3 tools/import_phonemes.py prepped/ --dialect ssbe --voice reference --dry-run
then again without --dry-run, listen at #audit, mark Good, export the
flags file and commit it. Nothing plays for a learner until the exact
dialect/voice/slug id is in APPROVED_PHONEMES.
General guidance: quiet room, consistent mic distance, no added vowel
after consonants, no trailing breath. A syllable demonstration must
sound like a syllable ON PURPOSE - it is labelled as one in the app.
Entry order follows docs/PHONEME_RECORDING_LIST.md, because
tools/prep_phonemes.py --split names files BY THIS ORDER when it cuts one
continuous take - recording in a different order misnames every clip.
Syllable-demo frame: /ɑː/ - the aCa frame is /ɑːCɑː/, the nam manifest's
/ɑCɑ/ in the only /ɑ/-quality this accent has. The spec's core list gives
it as "broad BATH /ɑː/" and the entries file carries it as
palm_bath_vowel, so it is in the inventory. It is long and BACK, so it
does colour neighbours: listen for a darkened /l/ or a backed /k/ and re-
take.
Cast a present-day Standard British speaker (professional register,
contemporary - not a trained RP stage voice). The spec calls this target
"the British English of present-day film, TV and everyday professional
life".
They must own all five core markers as their own speech, not as imitation:
the non-rhotic skeleton (broad BATH, rounded LOT, GOAT), steady SQUARE
/ɛː/, GOOSE far forward, tense happY /i/, open lowered TRAP.
Biggest thing to avoid in the booth: booth-careful articulation sliding
into Traditional RP - SQUARE regliding to [eə] and happY going lax [ɪ].
Spot-check those two takes first.
Second-biggest: register drift the other way. Keep [t] fully articulated
in t_syllable; the glottal is a realization of /t/ and has its own clip.
SHARE RULE. Most of these sounds are the same in every course, so one take
is recorded and copied into each. That is NOT safe for every entry: where an
accent's own published spec names a departure, that accent records its own.
Each entry carries "take": "shared" or "accent-specific" - never reuse
another course's file for an accent-specific one.
Accent-specific in Standard British (3): trap_vowel, goose_vowel, near_diphthong

entries.guidance: Controlled voiceless sustain /fff/, ~1s, lower lip to upper teeth. No vowel before or after.
Voiced sustain /vvv/, ~1s, buzz audible throughout. No added vowel.
Voiceless dental sustain /θθθ/, ~1s, tongue against the top teeth. No vowel before or after.
Voiced dental sustain /ððð/, ~1s - tongue against the top teeth, voicing on throughout. No added vowel.
Controlled voiceless sustain /sss/, ~1s. No vowel before or after.
Voiced sustain /zzz/, ~1s, buzz audible throughout. No added vowel.
Voiceless sustain /ʃʃʃ/, ~1s, postalveolar with light lip rounding. No vowel before or after.
Voiced sustain /ʒʒʒ/, ~1s - the sound in the middle of measure, buzz throughout. No added vowel.
Voiceless glottal breath /h/, ~1s of audible airflow, no voicing. Nothing after it - no 'huh'.
Hummed /mmm/, ~1s, lips closed the whole time. No vowel before or after.
Sustained /nnn/, ~1s, tongue tip on the alveolar ridge throughout. No added vowel.
Sustained velar /ŋ/, ~1s - back of the tongue up, no [g] release at the end and no added vowel.
Clear [l] sustained ~1s, tongue tip on the ridge, air round the sides. Do not vocalise toward [o] - that is a variable, not the target.
Sustain the approximant [ɹ], ~1s, no tap and no trill. Non-rhotic accent: /r/ sounds only before a vowel, so use that onset quality.
Steady /ɪ/ as in kit, ~0.7-1s at stable pitch. Lax and stressed - no drift toward /iː/, and not the tense happY /i/.
Steady /e/ as in dress, ~0.7-1s. Keep it a monophthong - no FACE glide, and clear of the longer, opener SQUARE /ɛː/.
Open, lowered /æ/ as in trap, ~0.7-1s, close to [a] but kept front and short - not a clipped back PALM /ɑː/. Stay low: do not raise it toward /e/.
entries.takeWhy: ssbe core: Open, lowered TRAP, close to [a]

entries.guidance: Relaxed /ʌ/ as in but, ~0.7-1s on one position. Stressed and fuller than schwa - no drift.
Short lax rounded /ʊ/ as in foot, ~0.7-1s. Light rounding, and no drift toward the long GOOSE /uː/.
Short rounded /ɒ/ as in lot, ~0.7-1s. The rounding is the point - keep the lips rounded throughout, never a flat unrounded 'ah'.
Neutral unstressed schwa, short side of ~0.7s, low energy - the colourless 'uh'. Keep it central, no stress colour.
Tense but weak /i/ as in happy, city - short, ~0.5s, low energy. FLEECE quality at half FLEECE length; run it to 1s and it is just /iː/. Never the lax /ɪ/.
Tense /iː/ as in fleece, ~1s, steady - resist any onglide. Give it full length: happY /i/ is this quality without it.
entries.takeNote: General Australian records its own take of this sound; this one is the shared take

entries.guidance: Long open unrounded /ɑː/ as in palm, ~1s, steady - the broad BATH words take it too. No rounding toward /ɔː/.
Long rounded /ɔː/ as in thought, ~1s, steady rounding - a monophthong, no glide, and no drift toward the short /ɒ/.
Broad /uː/ as in goose but spoken far forward, closer to [ʉː], ~1s. Lips rounded, tongue central - forward of a back 'oo', never a fully front rounded vowel.
entries.takeWhy: ssbe core: Fronted GOOSE, broad /uː/ spoken far forward, closer to [ʉː]

entries.guidance: Long stressed /ɜː/ as in nurse, ~1s, steady and central. Non-rhotic: no r-colour, no final r. Must read clearly longer and stronger than schwa, not a stretched schwa.
Long steady /ɛː/ as in square, ~1s held on one position. SQUARE is a monophthong in this accent - no glide to schwa at all.
Full audible glide /eɪ/ as in face, ~1s - start near DRESS height and land near /ɪ/. Do not flatten it into one steady vowel.
entries.takeNote: Cockney records its own take of this sound; this one is the shared take

entries.guidance: Complete audible glide /aɪ/ as in price - start open, land near /ɪ/. The whole journey, ~1s, with the landing not clipped.
entries.takeNote: Cockney records its own take of this sound; this one is the shared take

entries.guidance: Full glide /ɔɪ/ as in choice, ~1s - start rounded and back, land near /ɪ/. Rounding on the start only.
Full glide /əʊ/ as in goat, ~1s - start on central schwa, not a rounded back vowel, then glide to /ʊ/. No pre-/l/ backing here.
entries.takeNote: Cockney records its own take of this sound; this one is the shared take

entries.guidance: Full glide /aʊ/ as in mouth, ~1s - open start, land rounded near /ʊ/. One smooth journey, no break in the middle.
entries.takeNote: Cockney records its own take of this sound; this one is the shared take

entries.guidance: Centring glide /ɪə/ as in near, ~1s - /ɪ/ into schwa, but lighter and shorter than RP's. Let it lean toward smoothing without arriving at a long [ɪː].
entries.takeWhy: ssbe variable: NEAR smoothing toward a long [ɪː] for some speakers

entries.guidance: Full centring glide /ʊə/ as in cure, ~1s - rounded /ʊ/ into schwa. Keep both targets audible, not one long vowel.
entries.takeNote: General Australian records its own take of this sound; this one is the shared take

entries.guidance: Syllable demo (stops and affricates cannot be sustained): a clean /ɑːpɑː/ - full closure and crisp release, never a standalone 'puh'.
Syllable demo: /ɑːbɑː/ with voicing right through the closure - a true voiced /b/, never 'buh'.
Syllable demo: /ɑːtɑː/ with a fully articulated alveolar [t]. The glottal [ʔ] is a realization of /t/ and has its own clip - keep this one [t].
Syllable demo: /ɑːdɑː/ - voiced alveolar /d/, closure then clean release, no 'duh'.
Syllable demo: /ɑːkɑː/ - clean velar closure and release, no 'kuh'.
Syllable demo: /ɑːgɑː/ - voiced velar closure with an audible release, no 'guh'.
Syllable demo: /ɑːtʃɑː/ - one affricate unit, closure into friction, not /t/ plus /ʃ/ and never 'chuh'. This is the sound in tune /tʃuːn/.
Syllable demo: /ɑːdʒɑː/ - one voiced affricate unit, never 'juh'. This is the sound yod coalescence gives duty /ˈdʒuːti/.
Syllable demo: /ɑːwɑː/ - rounded lips gliding through, a moving approximant, never a standalone 'wuh'.
Syllable demo: /ɑːjɑː/ - a clean palatal glide into the vowel, never 'yuh'. Coalescence belongs in tune and duty, not here.
Syllable demo of a realization, not a phoneme: [ʔ] is /t/ here. Frame shifts to /ˈɑːtə/ spoken [ˈɑːʔə] - glottalling needs an unstressed next syllable. No isolated click.
